references.text: The use of the word 'zanav' (to attack from behind/the tail) is also found here, where Amalek attacked the weak and lagging Israelites from behind.
A similar military strategy in which the enemy was pursued and none were allowed to escape, as at the conquest of Ai.
The Lord's promise to give the enemy into Israel's hand, using the same expression 'netanam YHWH beyadkem' (the Lord has given them into your hand).
Rahab's recognition that the Lord has given the land into Israel's hand, reflecting the same theological theme of God delivering the enemy.
The Lord gives Jericho into Joshua's hand, the same promise of divine victory and delivery of the enemy.
The Lord gives the enemy (Sisera) into Barak's hand, the same divine promise of victory in battle.
The Lord gives the Midianite camp into Gideon's hand, parallel to the promise of divine delivery of the enemy.
